# @visio/router design

An explicit route table on top of Solid Router 2. The routes file owns the tree, page modules own everything else about their route, and a Vite plugin keeps the two honest and splits each page into an eager `route` and a lazy component.

## Goals

1. One place to read the URL structure (`src/routes.ts`) and one place to read a page (its module). Nothing generated, nothing scanned.
2. Types from imports: a wrong path, a renamed file, a module without meta, a pattern that disagrees with the table all fail in the editor or in the build, with a message that names the fix.
3. Solid Router stays the router, as the primitive under this package. The package re-exports what an app uses of it (`query`, `formAction`, `useSubmissions`, `revalidate`, `liveQuery`, the router hooks and their types), and lint bans `@solidjs/router` in app code, so an app has one router import. Its typed `paths`, preloading on hover, `query`/`formAction`, single-flight mutations and the prerender crawl all stay Solid Router's. The package is a contract and a compiler, not a runtime of its own.

## The API

```ts
// src/routes.ts
export const routes = defineRoutes([
  page('/', () => import('./pages/home')),
  layout('/docs', () => import('./pages/docs/layout'), [
    index(() => import('./pages/docs/index')),
    page('/docs/:slug', () => import('./pages/docs/page')),
  ]),
  catchAll(() => import('./pages/not-found')),
  api('/api/report', () => import('./api/report')),
]);

// src/pages/docs/page.tsx
export const route = defineRoute('/docs/:slug', {
  preload: ({ params }) => getDoc(params.slug),
  meta: () => ({ title: 'Docs' }),
});
export default function DocPage(props: PageProps<typeof route>) { ... }
```

- `defineRoute(pattern, { preload?, meta, matchFilters? })` is the page's contract. `meta` is required, so a page without a title does not typecheck. `defineLayout(pattern, { preload?, matchFilters? })` has no `meta`: the page under it sets the head.
- `page(path, load)` accepts only a module whose `route` declares `path`: `PageModule<P>` requires `route: PageRoute<P>`, and a different literal is a type error at the call site.
- `layout(path, load, children)` nests. Children are written with their full patterns (so their modules type-check against them) and rewritten relative to the layout at both the type and runtime level, which is what Solid Router expects. A root layout, `layout('/', ...)`, keeps its children's paths as they are. `index(load)` is the page at the layout's own path; `Child<P>` only admits an index whose module declares `P`. A `catchAll()` may not: the table has one, at the top.
- `catchAll(load)` is `*404`, and its module must declare `'*404'` (`PageModule<'*404'>`). Its preload sets status 404 on the server before the head flushes, and its meta always has `noindex`. A catch-all inside a layout is an error (`CATCH_ALL_NESTED`, and a type error in `layout()`): the table has one catch-all, at the top. Until 2026-10-08 `defineRoutes()` also added a `/404` page from the catch-all's module, which the crawl wrote to `404.html` for static hosts; the static build is gone, and so is that page. `api(path, load)` is a request handler module, and `load` is required, kept out of the page tree and out of the client bundle. Its pattern takes `:param`, `:param?` and `*rest`; params come decoded, and a malformed escape is no match.
- `apiMiddleware(routes.api)` on `@visio/router/internal/api` answers the `api()` routes; `visio()` puts it last in the server's middleware chain, so a site never wires it. A site's own `src/middleware.ts` is `export default defineMiddleware([...])`, which types each function as `Middleware`, like `defineRoutes()` for the table.
- `defineRoutes(list)` returns `{ pages, api, pending, Router, paths }` and preserves literal types, so `paths` is fully inferred. It calls `createRouter` itself: a site ends `src/routes.ts` with `export const { Router, paths } = routes`, and has no `src/router.ts`. Until 2026-10-07 every app had that file for one line, `createRouter({ routes: routes.pages })`. It passes `preloadLinks: intentPreload()`: since 2.0.0-next.38 Solid Router preloads no link unless it is given a strategy, and a site's links preload on hover, focus and touch. Solid Router's path types give up past about 45 routes, so the lab exports only `Router` and writes its links as strings. Two routes at one path are reported by the plugin (below), not at runtime: the check needs only the literal paths, so it runs in the dev terminal and the build, not on every client boot.
- `PageProps<typeof route>` gives a component its params (from the pattern) and data (from preload).
- The public `page()`, `layout()`, `index()` and `catchAll()` take no `route` argument. The plugin appends the module's eager `route` to each call (below), and the functions in `table.ts` that the compiled table calls take it as the last argument. Tests import those from `src/table.ts`.

## Meta

`meta` receives `{ params, location, data }` and returns the page's `Meta`: `title`, `description`, `canonical` (also `og:url`), `image` (a URL, or `{ url, width, height, alt }` for the `og:image:*` tags), `type` (`website` or `article`, for `og:type`), `modified` (ISO 8601, for `article:modified_time` and the page's `lastmod` in the sitemap), `noindex`, `social`, `jsonLd` for `application/ld+json` scripts, and `tags` for more `<meta>` tags. A page does not set `og:site_name` or `og:locale`, which come from `site.name` and `site.locale` only, or `twitter:card`, which is `summary_large_image` whenever there is an image. `headTags()` turns it into head tags identified by their name or property, so a later registration replaces a tag instead of adding a second one; the canonical link and the scripts carry a key for the same reason (the head identifies a link by its href, so an unkeyed canonical would pile up across navigations). The page's meta sits over the site's defaults (`withSiteDefaults()`): `og:site_name`, `og:locale` and the social image from `site.name`, `site.locale` and `site.image`, a relative image URL made absolute against `PUBLIC_SITE_URL`, and, with the origin known, a canonical and `og:url` of the page's own path for every page that sets none and is not `noindex`. A page should not key its own tags against these. `headTags()` and `withSiteDefaults()` are not on the package entry; tests import them from `src/meta.ts`. The document's static `<title>` is only a fallback; the head registry replaces it.

`tags` is the one way to add a `<meta>` tag from data, such as a verification code from a CMS field. A tag that does not change goes in `src/document.tsx`. Each entry is `{ name, content }` or `{ property, content }`, and nothing else: no other element, no other attribute. The head identifies a meta tag by its attribute and its value, so the next page's tag replaces it. Some tags belong to a field of `Meta` (`description`, `og:title`, `og:image`, `twitter:title` and the rest of `OWN_TAGS` in `meta.ts`). A tag in `tags` with one of these names or properties is dropped, in any letter case and with either attribute, because `name="og:title"` beside the router's `property="og:title"` is a second tag, not a replacement. In dev the router warns once per name (`META_TAG_RESERVED`) with the field to set. A type cannot reject a reserved string from a CMS, so the check is the warning, which the smoke run reads.

Two tags that the router writes have no field that covers every value, so a page may set them in `tags`. `twitter:card` from the page replaces the router's `summary_large_image`, for a `summary` card. `robots` from the page is the only robots tag, for `noindex, nofollow` or `max-image-preview:large`, with one exception. When the page is `noindex`, or the deployment is not indexable, and the page's value has no `noindex` (or `none`), the router keeps its own `noindex` and drops the page's tag. So a page tag can add to a `noindex`, but it cannot lift it.

A layout has no meta, and the head reads the page's meta only. A tag for every page is a helper that each page spreads into its meta, with the data from the page's preload. There is no element other than `<meta>`, and no merge from layouts.

`absoluteUrl(path)` resolves a path, or a `paths.x()` result, against `PUBLIC_SITE_URL`, which `visio()` defines as `import.meta.env.SITE_URL`. JSON-LD needs absolute URLs. `withSiteDefaults()` uses the same function (`resolveUrl()`) for the image and the canonical. An absolute URL comes back as it is. Without the origin it returns the path unchanged, as `withSiteDefaults()` does, and gives no warning: a dev server without `.env` is normal, and a warning there fails the smoke run. A site that must not write a relative URL in JSON-LD checks the origin itself, as the site's home page does.

`data` is what the route's `preload` returned, settled: a promise is awaited, and the promise-valued properties of a plain object are awaited together (`Settled<T>`, `settle()` in `meta.ts`). The component still receives the raw return as `props.data`. So a page writes `preload: () => getDoc(params.slug)` and `meta: ({ data }) => ({ title: data?.headline ?? 'Docs' })`. `data` is `undefined` when the preload rejected on the client (see below), and its type says so. A preload returns the query it calls, never `void getDoc()`: the returned promise is what the route table marks handled and what `meta` waits for. The table wraps every preload (`handledPreload()` in `table.ts`) and marks the return handled at the call, and each promise of a returned object: Solid Router marks only its own `query()` promises, and the outlet and the head read the rest after the page module loads. Until 2026-10-12 only the outlet marked the return, and only once it had loaded the page. A promise of the preload's own, an async function that chains a read on the page's data, rejected before then, and the server exited: a draft request without `SANITY_READ_TOKEN` stopped the dev server for every tab. Every read a page makes starts in its preload, a read that needs the page's data too (Dependent reads, below).

A route option or a helper that reads `paths` declares its return type (`(): Meta =>` for `meta`). `paths` is typed from the table, and the table reads each page's `route`, so a return type inferred from `paths` is a cycle, and TypeScript gives `any` to `route`, `routes` and `paths` (TS7022). This is also true when `meta` or `preload` reads `paths` through a module helper or a `const`. Each attempt to break the cycle in the router's types lost a type: the pattern check, `props.data`, or `matchFilters`. The annotation keeps them all, and `visio/meta-return-type` reports a function without it.

The head is the router's job, not the page's and not the outlet's. The table keeps `meta` from the eager `route` next to `preload`. The `Router` that `defineRoutes()` returns wraps the one from `createRouter()`: its render-prop child gets a `RouteHead` before the app's own content, and that calls `useRouteHead(router)` once. It matches the current location with `matchChain()`, takes the last level, the page, and computes its meta from the page's `params`, the location and the settled return of its `preload`. This is the model of React Router's `<Meta />` and TanStack's `<HeadContent />`: the route declares the meta, and the router renders it from the current match. Any outlet then has the head: `<PageTransitions>`, or `props.children` in a site without page transitions. The page component is the module's own default, never a wrapper. Until 2026-10-06 the table wrapped it inside the lazy loader (`withMeta()`), and on hydration Solid's `lazy()` takes the server's preloaded chunk and never calls the loader. So the first page rendered with no head of its own, and its tags were gone after a navigation away and back (#194). From then until 2026-10-08 `PageTransitions` called `useRouteHead()` for each page it mounted, and a site that rendered `props.children` built with no head on any page and no message. `useRouteHead()` is not on any entry: only the router calls it, so a page cannot register its route head a second time. `RouteHead` also registers the site's icon links, on every page, when `visio()` defines them in `import.meta.env.VISIO_ICONS` from the artwork in `src/icons/` (`iconTags()`, `packages/visio/DESIGN.md`, Icons). Without the define it registers none. Each link has a key, because the head identifies a link by its href.

The head calls the page's `preload` itself, beside the outlet's call, because no outlet hands its data on. A preload returns the `query()` it calls, and `query()` gives a second call within five seconds the same promise, so nothing is fetched twice. The cost is the call: a preload with side effects of its own runs them twice, as it does already when a link is hovered and then clicked. The lab's preload case shows the calls. On the client the head reads the last settled meta, so the title changes when the new page's data has landed, not when its transition ends.

How the tags reach the document is the part that matters for crawlers. `useRouteHead()` settles `props.data` in a memo and computes the meta from it. It registers the tags twice on purpose. The title goes in as a tag whose text is an accessor: on the server the head registry evaluates it before the shell flushes and holds the flush while it is pending, so a head that reads preloaded data lands in the document itself. The other tags go in as a list, which the registry only evaluates when it commits the head, by which time the same data has settled. A tag list registered from inside a `<Loading>` boundary, or one that is still pending at commit, only reaches the browser through the script the stream appends after the document, which crawlers and link previews never run. A prerendered or cached page renders in `async` mode (`packages/visio/DESIGN.md`, In-order pages) and has those tags in its `<head>`; a `live` page streams and does not. That was the failure this design replaces, and the two things that do not work instead: seeding the router's query cache before the render (every `<Loading>` boundary then comes out empty, see the prerender guard), and suspending the page itself until the data lands (the same).

A preload that rejects must not take the app down from the head. The memos sit outside every boundary, and on the client a rejection there halted the reactive system, so a failed read on `/account` (no `SESSION_SECRET`) froze every page after it even with an `<Errored>` in the page (2026-09-27). On the client the data memo turns a rejection into a sentinel, and the meta runs without data; the page's own `<Errored>` shows the failure. A meta that throws on the client, with data or without (`data.title` when the preload resolved `null`), gives no head tags, so the page's own tags go, and warns in dev (`resolveMeta()`). The server keeps the rejection and the throw: the memo's value is serialized for hydration, a symbol fails that and seroval's error exits the process, and a rejected preload there only costs the page its title (the document's fallback shows).

Where the head registers matters on the server. A head registration outlives its owner, and the server renders a page's wrapper again while the page's chunk loads, disposing the first render. A head registered beside the page stays behind with a disposed memo that never settles, and its pending title holds the shell for ever: every page with a preload hung on the first request to a cold server. The router's render-prop child is mounted once per request, above every page and every lazy chunk, so the head registers there once.

## Dependent reads

A page's second read can need a value from its first: a feed whose search term is in the page document, a reference, a second API. When the page component starts that read, the new page shows an empty `<Loading>` for as long as the read takes. The lab's router case h measures it: the document takes 300 ms, the feed 600 ms, and the target shows without its feed for about 19 frames with a fade and about 37 with reduced motion.

The navigation's hold is Solid Router's, not visio's. Solid Router holds a navigation for the `query()` reads that start while it is in flight, and commits once those have landed. A read that the preload chains on the first one, in an async function or a `.then`, starts before the navigation commits, so the hold covers it. The lab case measures this with Solid Router's own outlet (`props.children`) too. A read that a component starts once the first value has rendered comes after the commit and misses the hold. Plain Solid 2 holds nothing on a signal write: a new `<Loading>` shows its fallback at once and then the whole waterfall together. This is Solid's design, not a bug: in a held navigation, the fallback of a new boundary lands with the rest of the new page (the Solid 2 cheatsheet), and the router cannot hold for a read that only exists once an earlier read has rendered. A waterfall is the page's to remove, so the fix is the preload.

Until 2026-10-12 this section said that a chain in the preload misses the hold too, and that a site that renders `props.children` had nothing to wait for it. The lab case was wrong: its preload chose the chain with `"chain" in location.query`. In the router's first preload call, the one the navigation holds for, `location.query` can give the query of the page the navigation leaves. It is Solid Router's `createMemoObject`: `has`, `ownKeys` and a key that was read before return memos that have not seen the new URL yet, and only a key read for the first time makes a new memo. So that call did not chain, and only a later call outside the hold did. A property read (`location.query.chain`) fails the same way after an earlier visit has read the key. `location.search` is a plain value of the new URL, so a preload reads a search parameter with `new URLSearchParams(location.search)`, and lint rejects `location.query` there (`visio/no-preload-query`). `params` is a new object for each route context and is correct in that call.

visio closes the part it owns:

- The preload starts the dependent read, chained on the first, and returns it beside the page data. `Settled` awaits each property, so `meta` and `props.data` stay typed.
- `<PageTransitions>` waits for the same settled data (`settle()` from the `internal/outlet` entry) before it shows the new page. Until 2026-10-12 it waited only for a preload that returned a promise, so the promises of an object return were not awaited. A skipped navigation (`skip`, reduced motion) now waits too, with no handlers: it swapped the pages at once, and so showed the empty page.
- In dev in the browser, `query` from `@visio/router` is Solid Router's wrapped (`late-read.ts`). A read that a component starts within 500 ms after a navigation to another path committed, that is still pending 50 ms later, and that no preload asked for in the last five seconds warns `QUERY_NOT_PRELOADED` with the query's name and arguments, once per key. `RouteHead` marks the commit, from an effect on the pathname that exists on both sides in dev, so the hydration ids stay in step. The route table wraps each preload in dev, so a read it starts, or one that starts with no reactive reader (a `.then` or an async function in the preload), counts as preloaded. 500 ms covers a page module that still loads after the commit; 50 ms leaves out a read that shows its fallback for a frame or two at most. A layout's own read that depends on the path also warns: it belongs in the layout's preload for the same reason. In production `query` is Solid Router's own.

## Prerender

`router(wiring, reserved, facts)` adds the `prerender-crawler` plugin to every build (`prerender.ts`) in its `hybrid` mode, starting at `/`, configured with what every visio site needs: `serverFunctions()` from `@solidjs/prerender` with its defaults (it records which `prerendered()` reads the crawl called, for the Vercel output to cache), the boundary guard and the head guard below, and `robots.txt` (lets every crawler in and names the sitemap when there is one; a `robots.txt` in `public/` wins; a non-indexable deployment is not blocked there, since a crawler that may not fetch a page never sees its `noindex`). `wiring.robots` adds rules to the file: `visio()` passes the AI crawler rules of `@visio/aeo` there for an indexable build. The router writes the file, and the package that knows the crawlers gives the lines, so the router knows no crawler by name. The dev server answers `/robots.txt` with the same text, the `wiring.robots` rules included, from the router plugin's `configureServer` (`robotsMiddleware()`), before the SSR handler, which would answer with the 404 page. It has no `Sitemap` line, because only the crawl writes the sitemap. A `robots.txt` in `public/` wins there too: the middleware passes the request to Vite. A site sets nothing about the crawl. `wiring` is for `visio()`, the only caller: the origin of the sitemap, which it derives from `site`, a filter for the Studio's paths, the extra `robots.txt` rules, and `llms.txt` and the deploy output as extra integrations. The crawler's other options, `redirects` among them, are not exposed. Until 2026-10-10 a site passed seed `pages` and a `filter` through `visio({ prerender })`. The router writes the sitemap itself (`lateSitemap()`): the same pages as prerender-crawler's `sitemap()` picks (`indexable()`), sorted, with the page's `lastmod`, and an `xhtml:link` for each `hreflang` link in the page's head, so a site with `@visio/i18n` lists each page's language versions there too. The crawler's has no alternates. Without them the file is the crawler's, byte for byte (`meta.test.ts`).

**Pending routes.** `defineRoutes(list, { pending: ['/about', '/work/:slug'] })` lists pages the site links to before they exist. The crawl fails on a link without a page, so it skips a path that is pending or matches a pending pattern. The plugin reads the list from the source, so it must be an array of literal paths (`PENDING_NOT_STATIC`). Each entry is a warning in the build (`ROUTE_PENDING`), not in the dev terminal: a planned page is no fault, and the smoke run fails on every warning there. An entry whose page is in the table, or whose pattern takes in a static page, is an error (`PENDING_HAS_PAGE`): the crawl would skip that page, and the list cannot outlive its pages. At runtime the list does nothing: a pending path answers with the catch-all's 404.

**Route facts.** When the plugin reads the table, it fills `RouteFacts`, an object `visio()` holds: `pending`, for the crawl's filter; `cached`, the full patterns of every `page()` and `index()` that is not inside `live`; `uncached`, the `live` pages and the `api()` routes, which no cached pattern may take in; and `api`, the `api()` routes alone, so the Cloudflare Worker's `observe` hook does not call one a page (`cloudflare/DESIGN.md`, Observe). The deploy output caches by route with them. Since the build reads `live` from the source, the options of `defineRoutes()` must be an object literal with no spread (`OPTIONS_NOT_STATIC`) and `live` an array literal (`LIVE_NOT_STATIC`): a list the build could not read would put live pages in the cache (`packages/vercel/DESIGN.md`). `patternSource()` turns a pattern into a regular expression source for both: `:x` is one segment, `:x?` may be left out, `*rest` takes any number of segments, and every group is non-capturing. It matches a narrower set than Solid Router's matcher, never a wider one.

The crawl learns the routes nothing links to from the router: `RouteHead` announces the table's static pages (`solidRouterPages` from `@solidjs/prerender`) on the crawl's hint header (`announce.ts`). An extension's `announced` can keep a page out of that list, and its `head` can announce more paths from the page's data, which the router adds to the header after the meta resolves. A route's `announce` gives the params of the pages of a dynamic route; `crawlMiddleware` (`crawl.ts`, first in `visio()`'s chain) calls every one on the crawl's request for `/`, where every crawl starts, after the page is rendered, so a query in it delays no page and runs once a crawl. Each runs at its entry's full path, built from `path` as the tree is walked, not from `pattern`, which an extension's copy of an entry keeps (a language's page under `@visio/i18n`), with that entry's extension args (`lang`). A rejection fails the crawl (`ANNOUNCE_FAILED`), and so does a param missing from the pattern (`ANNOUNCE_PARAM_MISSING`): a sitemap that silently lacks pages is the bug it exists to fix.

An entry may also give the page's head facts (`AnnounceFacts`: `title`, `description`, `modified`, `noindex`, and an extension's own, `translations` with `@visio/i18n`), from the query that lists the pages. They are for the sitemap and `llms.txt` served live after a publish (#366): one read per route there, where a head per page would cost one read per page, and the Workers free plan gives 10 ms of CPU and 50 subrequests to a request. `meta()` stays the source. The crawl renders every announced page anyway, so `crawlMiddleware` puts the list with its facts on `/`'s response (`x-visio-announced`, URI-encoded JSON, as a header takes no character above U+00FF), and `announceCheck()` (`announce-check.ts`) compares each fact with the page's head and fails the build on a difference (`ANNOUNCE_HEAD_DIFFERS`). A fact the entry leaves out is not checked. A param with a fact's name would be hidden by it, so it fails the crawl (`ANNOUNCE_PARAM_RESERVED`). The language versions come from the extension's `alternates` hook (Extensions). The lists the crawl writes (the sitemap, `llms.txt`) are as of the build; with a route that announces, the server answers them live (`visio/DESIGN.md`, Live lists). Until 2026-10-08 `PageTransitions` did it, so a site with another outlet lost every page nothing linked to.

The boundary guard (`boundaries.ts`) is why the crawl is wired here at all. A page can be written without the content of a `<Loading>` boundary, and the response is still a 200. The crawl renders in Solid's `async` mode (`packages/visio/DESIGN.md`, In-order pages), where a boundary that never settles keeps its `<template id="pl-KEY">` placeholder, and a boundary that throws is written empty, even with an `<Errored>` around the `<Loading>` (only an `<Errored>` inside it writes its fallback). Only the hydration data tells the browser: it rejects the boundary's `KEY_fr` promise. The guard reads every rendered page in `teardown`. It finds placeholders with no content, and it runs the page's data scripts in a `node:vm` sandbox to find the rejected `_fr` promises. It also knows the `stream` mode's form, where a template with a single space stands for an error. Then it fails the build naming each page and boundary. The known way to get an unresolved boundary is a `query()` the boundary reads that was already settled before the render began, from a `start.serverRenderSetup` hook or middleware; the route preload is where such reads belong.

The head guard (`heads.ts`) is there because a page without its head is still a 200. On the server, a `meta()` that throws, or a preload it reads that rejects, costs the page its head tags (see Meta), and the crawler writes it with the document's fallback title and no description or social tags. The guard reads every rendered page in `teardown` for the `og:title` tag that `useRouteHead()` registers on every page, marked `data-dh` by the head registry, so a tag written in the document shell does not count, and fails the build naming each page without it. Every page in the list means the app does not render the `Router` of `src/routes.ts`.

## The cache

`tagCache(tags)` and `purgeCache(tags)` (`src/cache.ts`) are how anything on the server reaches the cache in front of the pages: `@visio/sanity` tags each read with `sanity` and purges it on publish, and a site may do the same for data of its own. They read a `PlatformCache` from the request event, `visioCache`, which the deploy output puts there: on Vercel `vercelCache` of `@visio/vercel` with `@vercel/functions`, which `visio()` puts on the middleware chain, on Cloudflare the Worker of `@visio/cloudflare` with Workers Cache. Without one, in dev and during the crawl, both do nothing. So no package that reads data knows a platform, and a third deploy target adds one provider. The router owns them because it decides what is cached (Route facts).

## The plugin

`@visio/router/internal/vite` does three things in a `transform` hook. The hook filter admits only the routes file and the `?pick=` ids, so no other module enters the plugin.

**Splitting.** A static and a dynamic import of the same module collapse into one chunk, which is exactly what a route table needs to avoid: the `route` must load up front, the component must not. The plugin rewrites `page('/x', () => import('./pages/x'))` into an eager `import * as r from './pages/x?pick=route&lang.tsx'` plus `() => import('./pages/x?pick=default&lang.tsx')`, and answers each `?pick=` id with the module reduced to that export (`compiler/pick.ts`). The reducer keeps the picked exports, every top-level statement that is not a declaration (an `if`, a loop, a call, a bare `export * from`), and every declaration something kept refers to; references are collected by identifier name outside type positions, so a stray match keeps a little too much, never too little. The `&lang.tsx` tail keeps the extension visible to plugins that filter on it.

**Checking.** Before rewriting, the plugin reads each page module (`moduleFacts`) and reports, with file and line: a loader that is not `() => import('literal')`, a path that is not a literal, a module it cannot resolve, a page without a default export or without `route`, a page declared with `defineLayout`, a pattern that differs from the table's, an index whose pattern is not its layout's, two routes at one path, and a table without a catch-all. The check has two steps. `collectRoutes()` reads the helper calls from the syntax tree, so an `import()` in a comment or a string does not count. The hook then resolves those loaders and reads the page modules, and `rewriteRoutes()` checks and rewrites with the result. Page modules are added as watch files. When one changes, Vite invalidates the routes module through that edge, and the check runs again. `PATTERN_MISMATCH`, `MODULE_NEEDS_ROUTE`, `PAGE_NEEDS_DEFINE_ROUTE` and `MODULE_NEEDS_DEFAULT` repeat what the types of `page()`, `index()`, `layout()` and `catchAll()` already reject; they stay as the safety net for a table that is not type-checked (a loader cast to `any`, a JavaScript file, a build that skips `tsc`).

A route under a path that an extension of `visio()` serves itself (its `served`, such as the Studio and the routes of `sanity()`) is an error (`ROUTE_RESERVED`): the server answers those paths before the table, so the route would never be reached.

Two routes at one path (`ROUTE_DUPLICATE`) are compared by full path, children joined to their layout's path the way `layout()` nests them. Param names do not count (`/a/:x` and `/a/:y` are one path), and an optional param counts as a required one (`/a/:x?` and `/a/:x` are one path too). A route whose module declares match filters is left out, since the filters can tell two such routes apart, and so is one whose options the syntax does not show. API routes are compared among themselves. The `live` list takes part too.

A page file that no route loads (`ROUTE_UNUSED`) is a warning. The plugin has no pages option: the pages folder is the deepest folder that holds every module the table loads for a page, layout, index or catch-all (`src/pages` in both apps), and it is not scanned when that would be the project root. Each check of the table lists the folder's source files, reads the ones the table does not load, and reports each that declares its route with `defineRoute()` or `defineLayout()`, so a component file next to the pages is never reported. A file written later is not in the module graph, so in dev the file watcher checks it on add and on change. Warnings print once, not once per environment.

**Live routes.** `defineRoutes(list, { live: [...] })` holds the routes that need a server: pages that read a session or per-request data, and API routes. They are ordinary entries of the table, and a live page's preload marks its server render `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, so no deploy output caches it. Until 2026-10-08 a static build removed the list from the source, so the list had to be an array literal (`LIVE_NOT_STATIC`) and a link to a live page checked `import.meta.env.PRERENDER_MODE`; neither is needed now.

**Environments.** In the client build the `api()` loader is removed from the call, so handler modules and whatever they import never become client chunks. The plugin also adds itself to `ssr.noExternal`: an externalised copy would import `solid-js` through Node and get a second Solid instance, and `useHead` would then miss the app's context.

Without the plugin the same calls still run: `page()` builds the preload as a function that loads the module first. The table then has no match filters, which only the eager `route` carries. Tests use that path; the site does not.

## Extensions

A feature that few sites use, such as pages in more than one language (`@visio/i18n`), goes in its own package, not in the router. The package plugs into seams of the router. A site that does not import the package bundles none of its code: the seams themselves cost about 0.5 kB (gzip) of loops in `defineRoutes()` and the head.

A site turns a feature on with one pattern, for the runtime and for the build: it imports the package and calls it. The runtime part goes in `extensions` of `defineRoutes()` in `src/routes.ts`, and the build part goes in `extensions` of `visio()` in `vite.config.ts`. No package is found by detection, and no import does something only because it is there. A package may have a build part only: `sanity()` of `@visio/sanity/vite` serves the Studio and its routes and writes the query types, with nothing in `src/routes.ts`. `packages/visio/DESIGN.md`, Extensions, lists what a build part may give.

**Types.** `@visio/router/internal/extend` declares six empty interfaces that a package fills with declaration merging (`declare module "@visio/router/internal/extend"`):

- `RouteArgsExtension`: fields of every page's props, preload args and meta args (`lang`).
- `RouteOptionsExtension<P, T>`: options of `defineRoute()` (`translations`).
- `EntryOptionsExtension`: the last argument of `page()` and `layout()`, one key per package. Without a package, the helpers take no such argument. Each helper has an overload without it, which types the entry's `options` as `never`: with one optional argument, TypeScript would infer it from the list that `defineRoutes()` takes, as the whole of `EntryOptions`. A type that reads `options` tests `[O] extends [never]` first.
- `PathsExtension<L>`: `{ paths: X }` makes `X` the type of `paths` of `defineRoutes()`, from the page tree `L`.
- `MetaExtension`: fields a page's `meta` may return besides the router's (`theme`). The router does not copy them into the head; the extension reads them from `meta()` in its hooks.
- `AnnounceFactsExtension<P>`: facts an entry of `announce` may give besides the router's (`translations`).

A declaration applies only in a program that imports the package. `test/extension.test.ts` type-checks a fixture site in a program of its own to prove this, and `test/types.test.ts` proves that the router's own program has none of it. The router's source must still type-check when a package fills the interfaces, since a site's program includes it.

**Runtime hooks.** A `RouterExtension` has these hooks, which `defineRoutes()` calls in the order of the list:

- `pages`: changes the page tree before the router is made. Each entry has `pattern` (the full path of the call), `options` (the last argument) and `route` (the module's route, with its extension options).
- `args`: the fields of `RouteArgsExtension` for an entry at a location. The router adds them to the meta args. To add them to the props and the preload args, `pages` calls `withArgs()`. To render an entry's component inside something of its own (a context), `pages` calls `wrapComponent()`, which keeps what Solid Router loads a lazy chunk through. These helpers are in the `extend` entry, so only a site with such a package bundles them.
- `announced`: `false` for a static page of the table that the route announcement leaves out; the crawl then renders it only when a page announces or links to it.
- `head`: for the current page, `locale` and `noindex`, tags of its own (`tags`, dropped when the page is not to index, and `always`, kept on every page: what the page looks like, not an address), `notFound` (status 404 and `noindex`), and `announce`, more paths for the crawl to render.
- `state`: what `root` gets for the current page, from its entry and its meta args. It is a memo of its own, not part of the head, so a `meta()` that throws does not change it.
- `root`: wraps the router's children, with the state as an accessor, for example in a context provider. A read of the state waits for the page's data, and no boundary is above `root`, so `root` passes the accessor down and never reads it. A component below a `<Loading>` reads it, the same on the server and in the browser.
- `paths`: the `paths` of `defineRoutes()`. With more than one, the last one's.
- `alternates`: the language versions of an announced page, from the `translations` its entry gives: each path with its `hreflang`, `x-default` included, as the page's head names them. The router calls the first extension that has it.

The plugin appends the module's route after the last argument, so the options come before it. `trailing()` tells them apart by the route's `path`, so the type of the options (`EntryOptions`) forbids a `path` key.

**Build hooks.** A `RoutesExtension` (in `visio()`, `routes` of an extension) has `sitePaths`, more full paths of a site that the duplicate check and the route facts count like its own, and `diagnostics`, checks that read the table, each site's full path and its module (`TableCheck`). A site's `options` node and a module's `defineRoute()` options node are on `RouteSite` and `ModuleFacts`, and the file's top-level statements are `RouteTable.body`. `@visio/router/internal/vite` exports the AST helpers the router's own checks use, and `collectRoutes`, `rewriteRoutes` and `routeFacts` for a package's tests. An extension may read the table with `collectRoutes` in its own build part too: `i18n()` reads the site's languages with it for `languages` of its extension. A diagnostic prints with the package's name. An extension may give a site's own path again; it counts once.

## Constraints

Same as the styling compiler: the runtime is plain TypeScript with no JSX (`createComponent` renders the page), and the source must survive Node's type stripping, so no enums, parameter properties or namespaces. Solid Router is a peer dependency; its `next` releases move, and this package is where a change lands once.

## Not yet built

- Match filters pass through to Solid Router but are not checked against the module.
- `meta` covers the common tags and extra `<meta>` tags; any other element goes through `useHead` in the page, and only outside a `<Loading>` boundary if it has to reach crawlers.
